question: Why might premature babies spend around 15 minutes a day hiccupping?
answer: Possibly to map their own breathing muscles. Recording 13 newborns, Kimberley Whitehead and colleagues at UCL found that each hiccup's sharp contraction of the diaphragm set off a large wave of brain activity, which may help the cortex learn where those muscles are. Preterm infants hiccup about 1% of the time. The jolt may be a lesson.
move: A glitch in a young system may be how it calibrates itself.
reference: Whitehead et al., Event-related potentials following contraction of respiratory muscles in pre-term and full-term infants, Clinical Neurophysiology, 2019
